messages.body_plain:
Dear Alex,

Sorry to bother you again, when I tried another version of methylKit, I installed it correctly. But when I tried to read BSMAP methylation ratio files into R via methylKit, I got another error which I do not know how to fix, I am just wondering have you ever see this error before?

Here's what I did:

--------------------------------------
1.python methratio.py -o sample.methratio.gz -d ref.fa -s samtools -z -u bamFile

2.
library(GenomicRanges)
library(methylKit)
library(mixtools)
library(data.table)
library(parallel)
library(edmr)

file.list <- list("sample1.methratio.gz", "sample2.methratio.gz")
myobj <- read(file.list,sample.id <http://sample.id>=list('case','control'),assembly="hg19",header=TRUE, context="CpG", resolution="base",pipeline=list(fraction=TRUE,chr.col=1,start.col=2,end.col=2, coverage.col=6,strand.col=3,freqC.col=5 ), treatment=c(1,0))

Then, I run into the error:
Error in scan(file = file, what = what, sep = sep, quote = quote, dec = dec,  :
  scan() expected 'an integer', got '0.000'
Calls: read -> read -> .readTableFast -> read.table -> scan
Execution halted
----------------------------

It seems like there's something wrong with the "read()" function of methylKit, but I am not sure. Now I try to remove the "-z" parameter in the first step, but I do not get the results yet. If this works out, I want to know is it OK for the following analysis (for example, the "edmr" package)?

Best wishes~
Yan

messages.subject: extracting per-sample methylation
messages.body_plain:
I would like to have a table of differential methylation stats as well methylation ratios for each sample so I can see how variable the samples are.

For stats, it's easy to convert methylDiff object to a standard GRanges object.

For ratios, the united methylBase object has all the required info, but the column names are sample IDs (not sample names) and methylation ratios need to be calculated. There is also the percMethylation() function, which produces a matrix of ratios with column names as sample names, which is just want I want, but that matrix cannot be easily be converted to GRanges to merge with stats.

Did I miss some function that can combine these two table types? Is there a recommended way to do this?

messages.subject: Re: [methylkit_discussion] extracting per-sample methylation
messages.body_plain:
If you want to combine everything in a GRanges object you can convert the methylDiff to GRanges, and use GenomicRanges::mcols() to add extra columns from percMethylation() output. The order of rows between methylBase and methylDiff should be the same so you can use cbind() on metadata columns of GRanges object.

Best,
Altuna

messages.subject: minimum read coverage always 10
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

I am using methylKit to read in sorted SAMs generated by Bismark, and I'm seeing that the minimum read coverage per CpG is always 10 across all samples, upon using getCoverageStats() and before filterByCoverage().  In the methylKit manual from November 2012, the histogram of CpG coverage does show the log10 of coverage starting at 1, so I'm wondering if there is some inbuilt functionality in methylKit because of which we see this behaviour.

I would really appreciate some clarification on this.

Thank you!
Rajat
